summary: Wi-Fi adapter disappears after SCCM imaging when driver rollback step runs on ThinkPad provisioning
description:
Issue summary: After running the SCCM task sequence for new Lenovo ThinkPad imaging (Windows 11, corporate image), we observe the Wi-Fi adapter object is missing from Device Manager and Network & Internet settings. This appears immediately after the 'driver_rollback' step (custom package) executes as part of the task sequence.
Impact: Affected devices lose wireless connectivity post-provisioning and require manual intervention to re-add the adapter or re-install drivers. This blocks onboarding and remote-first users who rely on Wi-Fi for device setup.
Environment: Corporate image built from SCCM TS v1.9, Windows 11 23H2, provisioning pool in prod-us-east.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot target device (Lenovo ThinkPad X13 Gen3) into PXE/CMI and start the SCCM task sequence 'Corporate-Win11-ThinkPad'.
2) TS applies image, runs driver injection, then executes custom package 'driver_rollback_v2' intended to remove incompatible factory drivers.
3) Continue TS to completion and first login on OOBE to corporate account.
4) Observe: No Wi-Fi adapter listed under Device Manager > Network adapters; Settings > Network shows no Wi-Fi toggle.
5) Reboot does not restore adapter. Manually running 'pnputil /enum-devices' shows no WLAN device entry.

Logs / Observations:
- SCCM TS log (smsts.log) shows 'Running step: driver_rollback_v2' then 'Code 0x0' for success.
- Driver removal script (preflight) uses pnputil /delete-driver by published name; evidence suggests it removed the preinstalled Intel AX210 INF and also the newer driver package supplied by driver injection.
- Device Manager shows a hidden 'Unknown device' entry under Other devices on some machines.
- No Event Log entries with clear driver install failures; WDI reports generic NIC not found (EventID: 35) on affected machines.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Collected smsts.log, driver_rollback_v2 script and SCCM driver package manifest from CM console.
Reproduced on lab X13 Gen3: removing driver_rollback_v2 from TS results in Wi-Fi adapter present (injected Intel AX210 driver). Re-introducing rollback removes adapter.
Ran pnputil /enum-drivers on affected device: shows no INTEL driver entries; pnputil /enum-devices lists no net adapters on PCI bus.

Checked driver_rollback_v2 contents: script removes INF entries matching 'oem*' and deletes driver store .inf by published name. It currently matches on substring 'Intel(R) Wi-Fi' which over-matches and removes both factory and SCCM-injected packages.

Hypothesis: rollback step overaggressively deletes driver store entries by substring and may remove device nodes that were just injected, leaving hardware without a matching driver entry and Windows not enumerating the PCI ID correctly.
Workaround validated: skipping driver_rollback_v2 or modifying it to only target legacy Broadcom/Realtek vendor IDs preserves Intel AX210 and restores Wi-Fi automatically.
Ran 'devcon rescan' on affected device: no new hardware found until the correct INF is re-imported via pnputil /add-driver <inf> /install.
Checked SCCM driver package timeline: a new 'AX210-Driver-2026-03' was published 2026-03-09 and the rollback script was last updated 2026-03-05 — timing could cause race conditions.
Requested vendor INF from Lenovo OSS for second-guessing; pending response.
Filed a request with Platform Engineering to temporarily mark driver_rollback_v2 as optional in the TS for critical onboarding builds (CONFIRM in change control).

next_steps: Merge PR 142 after test coverage completes and schedule TS change during maintenance window 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC.
Add safer whitelist matching in driver_rollback_v2 and a dry-run log mode that outputs candidate INFs to SCCM artifact store for audits.
Create a short runbook for Help Desk: commands to detect missing WLAN device (pnputil /enum-devices, devcon rescan) and a one-liner to re-install INF from package cache.
Coordinate with Vendor (Lenovo) to confirm published INF names and avoid future mismatches.
Monitor provisioning logs for 72 hours after rollout and set label 'monitor-72h' on this ticket.
resolution: Workaround: temporary TS change to skip driver_rollback_v2 for affected pools; planned fix is whitelist-based rollback script change. Full fix scheduled for 2026-03-15 change window.
